title: call_tier_min returns the FIRST call band, not the LOWEST — a validator-legal two-call-band config desynchronizes the corroborator's life-safety merge guards and can silence an urgency-9 call
reasoning: Reproduced this session: AlertsConfig._validate_channel_bands accepts two call bands ([10:call, 9:call, 5:notify, 1:none]) because uniqueness is enforced on min_score only and the class-rank monotonic check passes on [2,2,1,0]. With that validator-legal config, call_tier_min returned 10 while AlertPolicy.band_for_urgency(9) returned CALL. Corroborator._phone_call_threshold (corroborator.py:252-263) feeds both the concrete-country gate (corroborator.py:284) and the acknowledged/failed_terminal absorption guard (corroborator.py:180-183), so an urgency-9 CALL-band article would bypass both guards, merge into an acknowledged event, and be silenced by its cooldown (_RETRY_LIFECYCLE_STATUSES preserves 'acknowledged' in _update_event, corroborator.py:367). That is a suppression-direction hole in a life-safety system whose prime directive is never missing a 9-10. Latent (shipped config/config.yaml has exactly one call band, verified), but the config surface legally permits it, nothing warns, and the fix is cheap (min() over call bands or reject duplicate channel_class at load). Medium is the correct severity: real, confirmed, suppression-direction, but requires an unusual operator-authored config to trigger.
evidenceRefs: check:repro run this session (validator accepted two call bands; call_tier_min=10; band_for_urgency(9)=call)

Both files auto-load into agent sessions (corroboration.md auto-loaded into THIS session), so a future agent honoring them could reintroduce the suppression gate this phase deliberately removed. The impact estimate is not overestimated. However, the remedy cannot be executed unilaterally: the owner's global rules make CLAUDE.md and instruction-file changes proposal-first, never applied without sign-off, and the corroboration.md rule file itself carries life-safety-invariant sign-off language. The owner must authorize (or perform) the rewrite of the CLAUDE.md critical-rules line and the corroboration.md overhaul - this is a human-consent decision, not an executor fix.

title: AlertPolicy's relation/already_alerted_at inputs are dormant on every live path — 2.3/2.6 suppression logic runs only in unit tests until Phase 3
reasoning: This is intended phasing, not an omission. Spec 2.10 defines EventDecision explicitly as 'the interface Phase 3's EventDeduplicator produces and AlertPolicy consumes', and Phase 3 req 3.1 is where _find_matching_event grouping is replaced by EventDeduplicator.decide(...) emitting real relations. Until then the three production call sites correctly pass Relation.NEW (corroborator.py:425, state_machine.py:788-792, harness.py:55), and production one-call-per-event/SAME suppression remains covered by the preserved legacy mechanisms (_user_already_notified, cooldown, _RETRY_LIFECYCLE_STATUSES). The 2.3/2.6 policy logic is unit-tested per this phase's acceptance tests (tests 2, 2b, 3 all pass). The corroborator docstring (corroborator.py:416-419) documents the deferral. No defect against Phase 2's requirements.

title: Hardcoded _FALLBACK_CALL_TIER = 9 in policy.py contradicts the 'nothing is hardcoded' rule
reasoning: Confirmed: policy.py:85 hardcodes _FALLBACK_CALL_TIER = 9 and call_tier_min returns it when no call band exists. Unreachable today - AlertsConfig._validate_channel_bands (config.py:324-328) rejects any band map lacking a call band, and test_thresholds_config_driven proves live behavior follows config - so this is not a functional 2.8 violation (no loadable config is ever governed by the literal). But it is a literal urgency threshold in code on a project whose CLAUDE.md mandates config-only thresholds, and if the validator is ever relaxed it silently becomes the live call tier. Low severity is correct (dead defensive code today); preferable fix is raising instead of returning a literal.

title: LOW-tier country NAMES don't resolve — a classifier emitting 'Ukraine'/'Moldova' as target yields UNKNOWN and fires a CALL instead of the intended LOW demotion
reasoning: Reproduced this session against the shipped config: resolve_country('Ukraine') and resolve_country('Moldova') return None (geography.low_tier_countries contributes only bare ISO codes to _country_aliases; only monitoring.target_countries/aggressor_countries carry name/name_native entries), so geo_tier('Ukraine') is UNKNOWN and at urgency >=9 AlertPolicy fails open to CALL (policy.py:150-153) instead of the intended LOW->NOTIFY demotion. The failure direction is safe for the prime directive (over-fires, never suppresses) - the geo_weighter module docstring documents unresolved-as-UNKNOWN as a deliberate choice - and exposure requires the classifier to disobey the ISO-code prompt mandate. But it partially defeats the phase's false-positive-call reduction for name tokens, and only HIGH/monitored names are covered by test_country_names_resolve_from_config. Low severity confirmed; fix is adding name aliases for low-tier countries via config.

title: _country_aliases() rebuilt from config on every resolve_country call
reasoning: Confirmed in code: resolve_country (geo_weighter.py:126) calls self._country_aliases() on every invocation, rebuilding the full alias dict from four config lists per token; event_tier/tier_for_affected/floor_for_event invoke it once per country per article. Config is immutable per process, so caching (instance attribute built in __init__ or cached_property) is safe and trivial. Pure efficiency waste with no correctness impact - Low, non-blocking.

title: The _EVENT_GATE_EXEMPT_TYPES none-band branch is never executed by any test — a typo in the exemption set would go green
reasoning: Confirmed by tracing every gate test this session: with the default dedup.min_event_urgency=5, every existing test exits _passes_event_gate at corroborator.py:79 (urgency below the gate: the urgency-3 'other' case, the gate=6/urgency-5 case, the gate=8/urgency-6 case) or at corroborator.py:81-82 (alert band: the urgency-5/6/10 cases including test_min_event_urgency_config_driven's is_military=False urgency-6 case). Line 83's 'result.event_type in _EVENT_GATE_EXEMPT_TYPES' membership check therefore never executes in the suite - it requires gate <= urgency <= 4, and no test lowers the gate below 5 with a none-band urgency. A typo'd type name in _EVENT_GATE_EXEMPT_TYPES would pass all 591 tests. The 2.13 acceptance-test letter is met; this is a genuine coverage gap on the deterministic exemption the spec calls load-bearing. Reviewer's suggested test (gate=3, urgency-4 debris_found is_military=false -> event; urgency-4 'other' is_military=false -> dropped) is exactly right. Low, non-blocking.
